draft.title: Companies and limited liability
card: A company is an incorporated business. It is a legal entity, which means it is treated in law as a person separate from its owners. The owners are called shareholders.
Limited liability means a shareholder can lose only the money they put into the company. If the company cannot pay its debts, their personal assets are safe.
cannot sell shares to the public. Its shares are held by a small number of people, such as a family.
can sell shares to the public. It is often listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX), where its shares are bought and sold.
draft.remember: A company is separate from its shareholders, who can lose only what they invested.

a.q: Which statement best describes a shareholder's liability in a company?
opts: They can lose only the money they invested
They must pay all the debts from their own assets
They are liable for debts up to a yearly limit
They are liable only if the company is on the ASX
a.why: A company is a separate legal entity, so its debts belong to the company. A shareholder risks only what they put in. The option about paying all the debts describes unlimited liability, which applies to sole traders and partnerships, not companies.
a.clue: The company is treated as a separate person in law.

b.q: Priya and her two brothers own all the shares in Ocean Tiles Pty Ltd. The company wants to raise money by selling new shares to anyone who wants to buy them. What is the problem?
opts: A private company cannot sell shares to the public
A company cannot issue more shares once it has started
Selling shares would end the owners' limited liability
Only a business with employees can sell shares
b.why: Pty Ltd means a private company, and a private company cannot sell shares to the public. To do so it would have to become a public company (Ltd). Limited liability stays in place for both kinds of company, so that is not the problem.
b.clue: Look at what Pty Ltd tells you about the company.

a.best: They can lose only the money they invested

b.best: A private company cannot sell shares to the public
